title: Most of a STAR answer is Action, and it never stops before the Result
takeaway: Keep context to a few seconds, spend 60% on what you did and why, and always land a result with numbers.
sources: Almost every weak answer gets this ratio wrong in the same direction: two minutes of context, twenty seconds of what they actually did, and no result at all.
The single most common failure in behavioural answers is an answer that just stops.

data.heading: The billing-job story, part by part
lines: S: Second engineer on a four-person billing team.
S: A quarter of invoices were arriving late.
T: I owned the fix end to end. Two weeks, no downtime.
A: I added timing instrumentation around each stage.
A: 80% of runtime was one N+1 query over 40,000 invoices.
A: I rewrote it as one batched join: 26 minutes to about 90 seconds.
A: Behind a feature flag, both paths ran for two nights.
R: Late invoices went from about 25% to zero.
R: I wrote up the N+1 pattern and two other jobs got fixed.

notes.note: Situation: be boring and be fast. About 10% of the answer.
Task: makes your scope unambiguous, and the constraints show the difficulty.
Action gets 60%: say I, not we, with specific decisions and trade-offs.
Result: never skip it. Numbers where you have them, then impact beyond the task.
